name: cat
description: Concatenates files and prints them to standard output; the default way to quickly view short files.

flags.description: Show all characters: tabs as ^I, line ends as $ (debugging whitespace).
Squeeze multiple blank lines into one.
Display $ at the end of each line.

examples.output:
First line of the file
Second line
examples.explanation: Prints the entire file to the terminal.
Numbers every line — handy when discussing a file or reading compiler errors.
Concatenates two files into a new one — the original meaning of the name.
Starts reading from the keyboard into note.txt; finish with Ctrl+D. A quick way to create a file without an editor.

about: cat copies each input file to stdout in order. With no file (or -), it reads standard input. For anything longer than a screen, use less; for the top or bottom of files, head or tail.
useCases: Feed a file into a pipe: cat file | program (though program < file is cleaner).
mistakes: Using cat on huge files and flooding the terminal — use less instead.
Useless use of cat: cat file | grep x works but grep x file is better.
warnings: cat > existing-file.txt truncates it immediately before you type anything.
